data.name: Bacchu
data.gender_notes: Bacchu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bacchus is the Roman god of wine, fertility, luxury, and theatrical performance. In Hindu mythology, Bacchus is known as Bhairava, the terrifying god of time and destruction. He is also associated with the auspicious god Shiva. The name Bacchu carries the meaning “Lord of Wine and Intoxication” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Bacchu usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of wine and intoxication and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the intoxicating power of the divine, leading to spiritual transformation through ecstasy.
data.etymology: Bacchu belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Wine and Intoxication.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bacchu total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Bacchu, also known as Bhairava in Hindu mythology, is a complex and multifaceted god. The name is derived from the Roman god Bacchus, who was the god of wine, fertility, luxury, and theatrical performance. However, unlike the Roman god, who was typically depicted as a jovial and reveling figure, the Hindu god Bhairava is terrifying and fearsome. He is often depicted as a dark, blue-skinned figure with multiple arms, holding a trident, drum, and skull cup. This fearsome image is a reminder of the cyclical nature of time and the inevitability of destruction.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Bacchu, or Bhairava, holds deep spiritual significance in Hindu mythology. Bhairava represents the destructive aspect of Shiva, which is an essential part of the cycles of creation and destruction. He is also a protector of the world, guarding against evil and destruction.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bacchu is a name derived from Lord Shiva's divine form Bholenath or Bhairava, signifying childlike devotion and innocence towards the divine. It symbolizes the playful, joyous, and mischievous aspects of the divine, encouraging lightheartedness and freedom.
